plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch-adjusted DESeq2
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is a bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples, salmon-derived, already summarized to gene symbols) with a balanced two-batch, two-condition design (6 treated vs 6 control, each batch holding both conditions). Because the batch is known and balanced, the correct approach is to put batch as a covariate in the DESeq2 design (~ batch + condition) rather than pre-adjusting counts, which would understate uncertainty downstream. The pipeline is: (1) blind-VST sample-structure QC to confirm no unexpected outlier or batch-driven separation before testing; (2) DESeq2 Wald test with the batch+condition design, minimal pre-filtering, apeglm shrinkage of the condition log2 fold change, independent filtering and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05, with full fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram) and NA-flag reporting; (3) an edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check on the same design and filtered gene set, reporting the overlap between the two methods as the high-confidence gene set, since 6 replicates per group is in the range where the two tools can disagree; (4) preranked fgsea enrichment on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human gene sets to give pathway-level context to the gene list; (5) a conditional GO over-representation step that only runs if at least ~50 genes reach padj<0.05 (a short list gives an ORA test no power), otherwise it reports the list size and defers to the ranked fgsea result. No transcript-level tximport step is included because the input is already an aggregated gene-level count matrix, not per-sample quant.sf files, and no effective gene length is available, so a goseq length-bias correction is not attempted and this limitation is stated in the QC step. Strandedness cannot be inferred here because no alignment/BAM files are part of the input; this is noted as a caveat inherited from the upstream salmon quantification, not something this plan can act on.
